en:
טָהוֹר, טְהוֹרָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; next word)
1) clean, pure; not subject to levitical uncleanness. Bava Metzia 86ᵃ שגופך ט׳ … נשמתך בט׳ (Manuscript בטהרה) thy body is pure, and thy soul expired with (the word) ‘pure’; Sanhedrin 68ᵃ.—Kiddushin 70ᵇ וסימניך טמא טמא ט׳ ט׳ and the sign (by which to remember which of the two families is of unblemished descent) is, that with the name of an unclean animal (raven) is unclean, that with the name of a clean animal (dove) is clean; Bava Batra 91ᵃ. Kelim III, 7 ובחרסית ט׳ and the person that touches the clay is clean (not affected by levitical uncleanness). Ib. IV, 1 ט׳ is not subject to levitical uncleanness; and see from—דג ט׳, עוף; בהמה טהורה a fish, a bird, a domestic animal permitted to eat. Chullin XII, 2. Ib. IV, 3 בטהורה טהור if it occurs with an animal of the clean class, the person is levitically clean; and see from—plural טְהוֹרִים, טְהוֹרִין; טְהוֹרוֹת. Kelim II, 1 פשוטיהן ט׳ the flat-surfaced among them are not subject to uncleanness.—Berakhot 2ᵇ שהכהנים ט׳ וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. מטוהרים) when the purified priests enter &c. Bava Metzia 61ᵇ; and see from

עֲרֵיבָה, עֲרֵבָה f. (עָרַב I; compare אַרְבָּא) [joined or plaited,]
1) trough, tub, kneading trough. Pesachim III, 2, see סֶדֶק. Kelim XV, 1 עֲרֵיבַת העבדנין the tanners’ trough; ע׳ בעה"ב the domestic trough (for kneading). Ib. XX, 2 עריבת פיסונות the trough for mixing mortar. Yadayim IV, 1 עריבת הרגלים the tub for foot-baths; and from

—2) boat, skiff. Yerushalmi Shabbat IV, end, 7ᵃ עריבת הירדן, see יַרְדֵּן; Kohelet Rabbah to I, 15. Pirkei Avot Zar. 40ᵃ ע׳ מליאה חביות a boat-load of vessels (containing fish-brine). Eruvin 88ᵇ; Tosefta ib. IX (VI), 18; and e.—plural עֲרֵיבוֹת, עֲרֵב׳. Kelim XXIV, 3. Ib. IV, 1; and e.

comments.he: חבית שנפחתה ומקבל על דפנה או שנחלקה כמין שתי עריבות ר' יהודה מטהר וחכמים מטמאין שמתחלה לכך נעשית להיות מוטה על צדה ומוציא מה שבתוכו לצדדין ואם היתה גיסטרא הרי זו טהורה שלא אמרו שירין לשירין אלא שירין לכלים איזו היא גיסטרא כל שנסדקין אזניה ואפילו אחת מהן נסדקה למטה מאזניה אע"פ שאזניה קיימות הרי זו כגיסטרא ואם מתחלה עשאה יד של אזנים נדונת כחבית היתה מוטה על צדה כמין קתדרא הוא הדבר כל המתקבל עמה מים בשעה שהוא מערה משקין לתוכה מטמא במגע ובאויר כל שאין מקבל עמה מים בשעה שמערה משקין לתוכה מטמא במגע ואין מטמא באויר.

sections.en: A potsherd that cannot stand unsupported on account of its handle, or a potsherd whose bottom is pointed and that point causes it to overbalance, is clean. If the handle was removed or the point was broken off it is still clean. Rabbi Judah says that it is unclean. If a jar was broken but is still capable of holding something in its sides, or if it was split into a kind of two troughs: Rabbi Judah says it is clean But the sages say it is unclean.
sections.he: הַחֶרֶס שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמֹד מִפְּנֵי אָזְנוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ חִדּוּד וְהַחִדּוּד מַכְרִיעוֹ, טָהוֹר. נִטְּלָה הָאֹזֶן, נִשְׁבַּר הַחִדּוּד, טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא. חָבִית שֶׁנִּפְחֲתָה, וְהִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת עַל דָּפְנוֹתֶיהָ, אוֹ שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה כְמִין שְׁתֵּי עֲרֵבוֹת, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין:

sections.en: If a jar was cracked and cannot be moved with half a kav of dried figs in it, it is clean. If a damaged vessel (gistera) was cracked and it cannot hold any liquid, even though it can hold foodstuffs, it is clean, since remnants do not have remnants.
sections.he: חָבִית שֶׁנִּתְרוֹעֲעָה וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לְהִטַּלְטֵל בַּחֲצִי קַב גְּרוֹגָרוֹת, טְהוֹרָה. גִּסְטְרָא שֶׁנִּתְרוֹעֲעָה וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת מַשְׁקִין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת אֳכָלִין, טְהוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין שְׁיָרִין לִשְׁיָרִין:

en:
אֹזֶן, אוֹזֶן m. (Biblical Hebrew; √אז to be pointed, cut, compare חז, גז. see אוּדְנָא)
1) ear. Bava Kamma 79ᵇ א׳ של מַטָּה human ear, opposed Divine perception. Yerushalmi Shabbat I, 3ᵇ top; and from

—2) handle. Shir HaShirim Rabbah beginning ולא הי׳ לה א׳ וכ׳ but had no handle and could not be carried; and from—Du. אָזְנַיִם 1) ears. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 32, beginning א׳ לדרך
the road has ears (be on your guard in speaking); and from—2) handles. Kelim IV, 3, see גיסטרא; and from

—3) אָזְנַיִם or בנות א׳ swollen glands of the throat (Rashi). Pirkei Avot Zar. 28ᵇ א׳; Yerushalmi ib. II, 40ᵈ top; Yerushalmi Shabbat XIV, 14ᵈ top בנות א׳.

גִּיסְטְרָא, גִּסְטְרָא, גִּצְטְרָא f. (= גזרזרא, a reduplic. of גזר; for assimilation of sibilants compare Nöld. Mand. Gr. p. 45 sq.) something defective, mutilated ;
1) a large vessel which turned out defective or unwieldy, by having its handles broken off or being cracked, and is therefore used as a receptacle for refuse, as a pickling pot, as a receiver of drippings from a leaking vessel &c. Kelim II, 6 גס׳ שנמצאת וכ׳ (Arukh a defective vessel found in the furnace (in which vessels are put for baking); Tosefta ib. Bava Kamma III, 10 ואם היתה גסטרה but if the jug turned out a gistra, contradistinguished to נפחתה. Ib. אי זו היא גסטרא כל שנסדקין אזניה וכ׳ (Kelim IV, 3 גיס׳ כל שניטלו וכ׳ …) when is a vessel called gistra? When its handles are split (broken off) &c. Ib. 2 גי׳ שנתרועעה וכ׳ if a gistra is broken so as to be no longer a receptacle for liquids, though it may yet receive eatables, it is not susceptible of uncleanness, for there is no fragment of a fragment, i.e. a fragment of a gistra is no longer considered a vessel. Shabbat 96ᵃ (a leaking gistra is not considered a vessel) because nobody says הָבֵא ג׳ לג׳ bring a g. to be put under a gistra; and from

—2) an animal body maimed to disfigurement. Chullin 21ᵃ; 32ᵇ עשאה ג׳ נבלה if one made an animal a gistra by lacerating some of its limbs, it is considered a carcass. Ib. 52ᵃ ג׳ קאמריתו ye speak of a maimed body (a rib on each side disjointed)! Ib. 27ᵃ דלא לישוייה ג׳ that in cutting the animal’s throat one must not make it a gistra (by cutting the head off). Sanhedrin 52ᵇ דעביד ליה ג׳ that the culprit be cut in two.—Chullin 124ᵃ דעבדיה ג׳ he split the stove lengthwise.—plural גִּיסְטְרָאוֹת, גִּיסְטְרָיוֹת. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 8 שרובן מן הג׳ for most of the fragments of pottery found in the potter’s place come from misshaped vessels. Makhshirin II, 3 ג׳ שישראל וכ׳ pots into which Israelites and gentiles cast their refuse.—Yerushalmi Shabbat III, beginning 5ᶜ ממלא גִּצְרָא וכ׳ one may fill a large pot with hot ashes &c.

—3) (castra) camp, see גַּסְטְרָא.

נטי, נָטָה (Biblical Hebrew)
1) (compare נָטַע) to stretch; to pitch a tent. Yalkut Breishit 67 בתחלה נ׳ אהלה וכ׳ (Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 נטע) first he pitched Sarah’s tent &c.

—2) to hang over, incline; to decline. Makkot II, 7 ונופו נוֹטֶה, see נוֹף II; Kiddushin 40ᵇ. Nedarim IV, 5, and e. הנוֹטוֹת overhanging fruit. Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan III, 82ᵃ בנוֹטוֹת when one’s mustache hangs over the mouth.—Sanhedrin 6ᵇ להיכן הדין נוטה which way the judgment will incline (in whose favor the verdict will be). Ib. 3ᵇ (reference. to Shemot XXIII, 2) עשה לך בית דין נוטה arrange for thyself a court which can lean towards one side, i.e. of uneven numbers. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 96, and from נ׳ למות one inclines towards dying, feels death approaching; and see from

—3) to bend, pervert judgment. Mekhilta Mishpatim section (Parashah) 20 שמא תאמר … ואיני נוטה את הדין lest you say, I will take a bribe but will not pervert the law.—Part. pass. נָטוּי; f. נְטוּיָה; plural נְטוּיִים, נְטוּיִין; נְטוּיוֹת a) hanging over, threatening, inclining. Sanhedrin 109ᵃ קיר נ׳ a threatening wall; Rosh Hashanah 16ᵇ; and e.—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 49 נ׳ למות, see supra.—b) spread; pitched. Oholot VII, 2. Tosefta ib. VIII, 2; and e.

Hifil - הִיטָּה
1) (neut. verb) (neut. verb) to incline. Bava Metzia 59ᵇ הִיטּוּ כותלי וכ׳ the walls of the school-house bowed (threatening to fall). Ib. ועדיין מַטִּין ועומדין and so they still stand bending over. Berakhot 11ᵃ הִטֵּתִי, see זָקַף. Ketubot 84ᵇ; Eruvin 46ᵇ מַטִּין one is inclined (in favor of R. Akiba’s opinion), i.e. the presumption is in his favor, opposed הלכה definite decision for general practice. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin I, 18ᵃ bottom of page (reference. to I Kings XXII, 19) אלו מטין לכף זכות וכ׳ these argued in favor, and those against. Rosh Hashanah 17ᵃ ורב חסד מַטֶּה וכ׳ and He who is abundant in kindness inclines (the scales) towards the side of kindness; and from

—2) to decline, move sideways. Ketubot 10ᵃ a man walking in the dark, ה׳ מצאו פתוח if he moves sideways (towards the door), he finds it open, if he does not (but strikes against the door) &c.—Transferred to perform coition without violently tearing the hymen. Ib.

—3) (act. verb) to bend; ה׳ דין to wrest judgment. Mekhilta l. common gender. שלא תאמר … אַטֶּה עליו את הדין say not, because he is a wicked man, I will turn the verdict against him. Peah VIII, 9 כל דיין … ומַטֶּה את הדין a judge that takes a bribe and perverts judgment; and from

—4) (after Shemot XXIII, 2) to decide by majority (compare כָּרַע). Sanhedrin IV, 1 דיני ממונות מטין וכ׳ in civil law a majority of one decides in favor or against (the claimant), ודיני נפשות מטין וכ׳ in criminal law a majority of one decides in favor of the defendant, but for a verdict against the defendant a majority of two is required, see הַטָּיָה. Mekhilta l. common gender. הרוג על פי מטין put to death on a majority vote; מה עדים … אף מטין בשנים as incriminating witnessess must be two, so must the majority be two.—Part. pass. מוּטֶּה; f. מוּטָּה reclining, bending over. Moʿed Katan 21ᵃ; Yevamot 103ᵃ בין עומד … בין מ׳ standing, sitting or reclining. Kelim IV, 3; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 10 היתה מ׳ על צדה וכ׳ if the vessel was misshaped so as to bend sideways like a sedan chair. Ib.; ib. 5 מַטָּה על צדה.—V. מוּטָּה.

צִידוֹן, צַיְדָן, צַיְי׳ proper noun of a place (Biblical Hebrew צִידוֹן) Zidon, Sidon (Zaidan), in Phœnicia. Tosefta Demai I, 10; Yerushalmi ib. I, 22ᵃ bottom of page צידן. Tosefta Eruvin VI (V), 8; Yerushalmi ib. V, 22ᵇ bottom of page Tosefta Yevamot XIV, 7 אבא יודן איש צידן Abba Judan of Z. Gittin VII, 5 צידן (Yerushalmi ed. ציי׳). Tosefta Zevachim I, 5 בצידן (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) ציידין, read: בצ׳); and see from—Denom. צִידוֹנִי m.; plural צִידוֹנִיִּים, צִידוֹנִיִּין. Midrash Samuel Chaldaic XXIII אבא צ׳ Abba of Z.—Kelim IV, 3 הצידניים ed. Dehr. (ed. הצדוניים); Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 11 הצידו׳.—Chaldaic צַיְדַנְיָא, צַיְדַנְיָיה, צַיְי׳. Yerushalmi Yevamot IX, beginning 10ᵃ ר׳ יוסי צ׳; Yerushalmi Nazir VII, end, 56ᵈ; ib. 56ᶜ ר׳ צ׳ (insert יוסי); Yerushalmi Terumot XI, end, 48ᵇ צירניא (correct accordingly).

קְתִדְרָא, קְתִדְרָה, קְתִידְ׳ f. (καθέδρα) a soft seat, chair with back. Ketubot V, 5 ארבע יושבת בק׳ (not ארבעה) if the wife brought four maids, she may sit in the chair (need not do any house work). Ib. 61ᵃ. Kelim IV, 3 כמין ק׳ (Mishnah ed. רָה …) in the shape of a cathedra (with a curved or hollow back). Ib. XXIV, 2 העשויה כק׳ a wagon seat formed like a cathedra. Eicha Rabbah to I, 1 ק׳ (רבתי) בכל מקום … מציעין לו wherever one of the sons of Jerusalem came to a country place, they spread for him a cathedra to sit on it, in order to hear his wisdom. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Vayḥi, p. 7ᵇ (reference. to I Kings X, 19) כהדא ק׳ דמשה like the seat of Moses (see Revue des Ét. Juives XXXIV, p. 99, sq.); Esther Rabbah to I, 2 קדירתא דדרניש (read: קתידרא); Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 43 ק׳ עשו לו כק׳ וכ׳ they made for him (Moses) a seat like the scholars’ cathedra in which one sits and yet seems to be standing; and e.—plural קְתִדְראוֹת, קְתִדְרָיוֹת, קְתִיד׳. Yerushalmi Sukkah V, beginning 55ᵃ ושבעים ק׳ וכ׳ seventy gilt chairs were there (in the synagogue of Alexandria), beset with precious stones &c.; Bavli Sukkah 51ᵇ; Tosefta ib. IV, 6 שבעים ואחת ק׳. Yerushalmi Berakhot VI, 10ᵈ top; and e.

קוֹס m. (קסס, compare כסס, and קוץ) [cutting,] a rough-edged cup.—plural קוּסִּים or קוֹסִים. Kelim IV, 3 ק׳ הצידוניים Sidonian cups; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 11 קיסום ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (correct accordingly).

קוּרְפָּיוֹת f. plural a kind of cups or bowls with pointed bottoms. Kelim IV, 3 (Rabbenu Shimshon קַרְפָּאוֹת; Arukh קִירְפָּ׳); Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 11 קַפְרָאוֹת ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant קרפאות).

comments.he: חבית שנפחתה ומקבל על דפנה או שנחלקה כמין שתי עריבות ר' יהודה מטהר וחכמים מטמאין שמתחלה לכך נעשית להיות מוטה על צדה ומוציא מה שבתוכו לצדדין ואם היתה גיסטרא הרי זו טהורה שלא אמרו שירין לשירין אלא שירין לכלים איזו היא גיסטרא כל שנסדקין אזניה ואפילו אחת מהן נסדקה למטה מאזניה אע"פ שאזניה קיימות הרי זו כגיסטרא ואם מתחלה עשאה יד של אזנים נדונת כחבית היתה מוטה על צדה כמין קתדרא הוא הדבר כל המתקבל עמה מים בשעה שהוא מערה משקין לתוכה מטמא במגע ובאויר כל שאין מקבל עמה מים בשעה שמערה משקין לתוכה מטמא במגע ואין מטמא באויר.

שולי הקרפאות ושולי הקיסום הצידוניים וכלי חרש ששוליו חדים וכדברי ר' נתן הקוז והקוד הבבלי שנסדקו מלמעלה ומקבלין כשיעור מלמטה אע"פ שאינן יכולין לישב שלא מסומכין טמאין שלכך נעשו מתחלתן שולי כלי עצים וכלי זכוכית וכלי עצם קרטיסין שפן ועשאן ומקבלין כל שהן טמאין היה שוות מן השפה הפנימית ולפנים הימנה ולחוץ טהורה כלי חרש מקבלין טומאה משתגמר מלאכתן דברי ר"מ ר' יהודה אומר משיצרפו בכבשן צרפן אפילו בגפת טמאה ואינו חושש שמא מיצה משקין ומשם רשות עם הארץ אין חושש להן וחבירתה אפילו בא לאחר שלשה ימים ונוטל.

sections.en: What is meant by a "damaged vessel" (gistera)? One whose handles were removed. If sharp ends projected from it: Any part of it which can contain olives contracts impurity by contact, while any impurity opposite an end conveys impurity to the vessel through its air-space, But any part of it which cannot contain olives contracts impurity by contact, while an impurity opposite an end does not convey impurity through its air-space. If it was leaning on its side like a kind of cathedra, Any part of it which can contain olives contracts impurity by contact, while any impurity opposite an end conveys impurity to the vessel through its air-space, But any part of it which cannot contain olives contracts impurity by contact, while an impurity opposite an end does not convey impurity to the vessel through its air-space. Bowls with Korfian [bottoms], and cups with Zidonian bottoms, although they cannot stand unsupported, are susceptible to impurity, because they were originally fashioned in this manner.
sections.he: אֵיזוֹ הִיא גִסְטְרָא, כֹּל שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ אָזְנֶיהָ. הָיוּ בָהּ חִדּוּדִין יוֹצְאִין, כֹּל הַמְקַבֵּל עִמָּהּ בְּזֵיתִים, מִטַּמֵּא בְמַגָּע וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר. וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל עִמָּהּ בְּזֵיתִים, מִטַּמֵּא בְמַגָּע וְאֵין כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר. הָיְתָה מֻטָּה עַל צִדָּהּ כְּמִין קַתֶּדְרָה, כֹּל הַמְקַבֵּל עִמָּהּ בְּזֵיתִים, מִטַּמֵּא בְמַגָּע וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר. וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל עִמָּהּ בְּזֵיתִים, מִטַּמֵּא בְמַגָּע וְאֵין כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר. שׁוּלֵי קוֹרְפִיּוֹת וְשׁוּלֵי קוֹסִים הַצִּידוֹנִיִּים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לֵישֵׁב שֶׁלֹּא מְסֻמָּכִין, טְמֵאִין, שֶׁלְּכָךְ נַעֲשׂוּ מִתְּחִלָּתָן:

en: סְפָי m. (סָפָה = Biblical Hebrew שָׂפָה) rim.—plural סְפָיוֹת, סְפָאוֹת. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. II, end, 42ᵃ; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma VI, 17 (not ספונאו׳), see אִסְטַגְיוֹת; Kelim VIII, 9 שְׂפָיוֹת. Ib. IV, 4 ספיות Arukh ed. Kohelet (oth. ed. Arukh סְפָאוֹת, סְפָאיוֹת; ed. שׂפָיוֹת).—סְפָיִין, Yerushalmi Shabbat VII, 10ᵈ top, see סִפָּא.

צָרַף (Biblical Hebrew; compare צרב) [to press, shrink,]
1) to smelt, melt; trnsf. to refine, purify, try. Yerushalmi Ketubot VII, end, 31ᵈ; Tosefta Ketubot VII, 11 צוֹרֵף נחשת, see infra. Yoma 72ᵇ (reference. to Psalms XVIII, 31) זכה משמחתו … צוֹרַפְתּוֹ if he deserves well, she (the Torah) cheers him; if not, she smelts him (through trials); צורפתו לחיים she steels him for life; צורפתו למיתה she smelts him for death. Yalkut Shemot 391 דרשתי … צָרַפְתִּי ובחנתי וכ׳ I studied and searched, refined and tested &c.; and from

—2) to tighten, harden. Yoma l. common gender., see supra. Yerushalmi Yevamot XVI, 15ᵈ top שצְרָפַתּוֹ Variant, see צָפַד.

—3) to change, see infra.

Piël - צֵרֵף
1) to smelt. Ketubot VII, 10 (among the occupations to which a wife may object) מְצָרֵף נחושת, explained ib. 77ᵃ חשלי דודי, see חַשְׁלָא; anoth. opinion מחתך נחושת וכ׳, see חָתַךְ; Tosefta ib. l. common gender. זה מתיך וכ׳ he that casts bronze.—Transferred to refine. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 44 (reference. to צרופה, Psalms XVIII, 31) לא נתנו המצות אלא לצָרֵף וכ׳ the (ceremonial) laws have been given for the purpose of refining (disciplining) men through them. Ib. שצֵרְפוֹ הקב"ה וכ׳ (Abraham) whom the Lord tried in the furnace of fire. Ib. (reference. to צֹרֵף, Isaiah XLI, 7) זה אברהם שצרפו וכ׳ that means Abraham, whom the Lord tried &c.; (Yalkut Isaiah 313 שנִצְרַף, Nifal).

—2) to tighten, harden. Makhshirin V, 7 המוליך … לצָרְפָהּ if one takes a ship out to sea for the sake of tightening it; מוציא מסמר … לצָרְפוֹ if one takes a (glowing) nail in the rain for the sake of hardening it; Tosefta ib. II, 16 בשביל לצוֹרְפוֹ. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 13 צֵרְפָן אפי׳ וכ׳ (or צְרָפָן) if he hardened (baked) them (the earthen vessels) even in a peat fire. Beitzah 32ᵃ משיְצָרְפוֹ בכבשן (Manuscript Munich משישרפו) from the time be baked it in the kiln. Bava Metzia 84ᵃ (of iron weapons) משיְצָרְפֵם בכבשן when he has hardened them in the furnace, see צִחְצֵחַ; and e.

—3) [to melt together, weld,] to combine, join. Ma'asrot II, 5 ואם צֵרַף (Yerushalmi ed. צירף) if he combined (ate them together). Yerushalmi Pesachim III, 30ᵃ top שני … אין הבית מְצָרף if two pieces (of leavened matter), each half the size of an olive, are in the same room, the room does not join them (so as to be counted one olive-size); if in one vessel, הכלי מצרף the vessel joins them. Kiddushin 40ᵃ, and e. מְצָרְפָהּ למעשה, see מַחֲשָׁבָה; and from

—4) to change small for large coin, opposed פָּרַט. Ma'aser Sheni IV, 2 כמות … שהוא מצרף as the banker counts when he gives small change for large coins, not as he counts when giving large coins for small change; Tosefta ib. III, 3 המְצָרֵיף … שמצריף ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant המצרף … מצטרף) if one buys a gold Denar for coins designated for second tithes, he must count as the banker would when selling small change, not as he would, when buying large change. Shekalim II, 1 מְצָרְפִין, see דַּרְכּוֹן. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia IV, end, 9ᵈ לצוֹרְפָהּ … מְצָרְפָהּ ביפה if he wants to change the defective coin to be spent in Jerusalem, he must exchange it as if it were of full value (see Bavli Bava Metzia 52ᵇ); and from—Sifré Devarim 48 אחד מצרף דינר ואוכלו ואחד מצ׳ דינר ומניחו one gathers a gold Denar and spends it, and another changes his accumulation for a gold Denar and puts it away; Yalkut ib. 873, see סָגַל.

Nifal - נִצְרַף
1) to be smelted, tried. Yalkut Isaiah 313, see supra. Midrash Till. to Psalms CXIX, 81 כבר נִצְרַפְנוּ we have already been tried.

—2) to be hardened. Kelim IV, 4 משיִצָרְפוּ בכבשן when they have been baked in the kiln; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma III, 13 משיִצְטָרְפוּ.

Hithpaël - הִצְטָרֵף
1) same
, see supra.—2) to be joined, combined, counted in. Nazir 35ᵇ, and e. אין היתר מִצְטָרֵף לאיסור a permitted thing is not to be joined to a forbidden thing, i.e. if one ate simultaneously, one half of the legal size each, of a permitted and of a forbidden thing, the two must not be counted together to make up the legal size. Ib. 4ᵃ מִצְטָרְפִים זה עם זה they are counted together. Ib. VI, 1. Berakhot 47ᵇ תשעה ועבד מִצְטָרְפִין nine freemen and one slave may be combined (to make up the requisite number of ten for prayers). Ib. שנים ושבת מצט׳ two persons (at meal) and the Sabbath may be combined (count for three persons); שני ת"ח … מצט׳ two scholars (at meal) who are engaged in discussion are counted as three. Mikvaot III, 4 מצט׳ are combined to make up the legally required quantity of water; and from—Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni III, 3, see supra.

GEMARA: Who is the tanna who taught that hollowing out a lamp is considered creating a vessel, even if it is not fired in a furnace? Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi Meir, as it is taught in a baraita with regard to the halakhot of ritual impurity: From when is an earthenware vessel susceptible to ritual impurity? It is from when its work is completed, i.e., when the clay has been made into the form of a vessel; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehoshua says: It is from when the vessel is fired in the furnace.

Abaye said to him: From where do you conclude that this is the same opinion? Perhaps Rabbi Meir stated his opinion only there, with regard to vessels, since they are fit to contain something. Although they cannot hold liquids before being fired in a furnace, they can contain other items. But here, for what use is this lamp fit? The Gemara responds: It can be used to contain small coins.

Some say the following version of the discussion: Rav Yosef said: The mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, as we learned: Ḥaraniyyot pots [ilpasin] are unfinished earthenware pots made together with their covers. The covers are removed after they are fired in a furnace. They are pure with regard to contracting the impurity of a tent over a corpse, as they do not have a receptacle. Earthenware vessels can contract impurity imparted by a corpse only if they have a hollow space that can contain something. But ḥaraniyyot pots are rendered impure by the carrying of a zav, even if the zav moved them without actually touching them, as this impurity applies to any earthenware vessels that serve some purpose.

Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says: These vessels are even pure with regard to the impurity imparted by the carrying of a zav because their labor is not completed; therefore, they are not fully formed. This implies that when the pots are completed, they are considered full-fledged vessels, even before they have been fired in a furnace.

Abaye said to him: Perhaps it is not so, as it is possible to say that Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, stated his opinion only there, in the case of ḥaraniyyot pots, since they are fit to contain something. But here, in the case of a lamp, for what is it fit? The Gemara replies: It is fit to contain small coins.

The Sages taught: One may not hollow out a lamp, and one may not create ḥaraniyyot pots on a Festival. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits creating ḥaraniyyot pots. The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of ḥaraniyyot? Rav Yehuda said: They are pots of a city [iraniyyot]. The Gemara again inquires: What is the meaning of iraniyyot? Abaye said: It means villagers’ bowls who will use even clay vessels that have not been fully formed or fired, as they are not particular with regard to half-finished utensils.
he: גְּמָ׳ מַאן תְּנָא דִּפְחִיתַת נֵר מָנָא הוּא? אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא: כְּלִי חֶרֶס, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבֵּל טוּמְאָה — מִשֶּׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מִשֶּׁיִּצְרְפוֹ בַּכִּבְשָׁן.
אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם אֶלָּא דַּחֲזֵי לְקַבּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ מִידֵּי, אֲבָל הָכָא לְמַאי חֲזִי? לְקַבּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ פְּשִׁיטֵי.
אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק הִיא, דִּתְנַן: אִלְפָּסִין חִרָנִיּוֹת — טְהוֹרוֹת בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת, וּטְמֵאוֹת בְּמַשָּׂא הַזָּב.
רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: אַף טְהוֹרוֹת בְּמַשָּׂא הַזָּב, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן.
אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק הָתָם, אֶלָּא דַּחֲזֵי לְקַבּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ מִידֵּי, אֲבָל הָכָא לְמַאי חָזֵי? לְקַבּוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ פְּשִׁיטֵי.

תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין אֶת הַנֵּר, וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין אִלְפָּסִין חִרָנִיּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַתִּיר בְּאִלְפָּסִין חִרָנִיּוֹת. מַאי חִרָנִיּוֹת? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: עִרָנִיּוֹת. מַאי עִרָנִיּוֹת? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: צָעֵי חַקְלָיָיתָא.

sections.en: An earthenware vessel that has three rims: If the innermost one projects above the others, all outside it is not susceptible to impurity. If the outermost one projects above the others all within it is susceptible to impurity; And if the middle one projects above the others, that which is within it is susceptible to impurity, while that which is without it is not susceptible to impurity. If they were equal in height: Rabbi Judah says: the middle one is deemed to be divided. But the sages ruled: all are not susceptible to impurity. When do earthenware vessels become susceptible to impurity? As soon as they are baked in the furnace, that being the completion of their manufacture.
sections.he: כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ שְׂפָיוֹת, הַפְּנִימִית עוֹדֶפֶת, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר. הַחִיצוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת, הַכֹּל טָמֵא. הָאֶמְצָעִית עוֹדֶפֶת, מִמֶּנָּה וְלִפְנִים, טָמֵא. מִמֶּנָּה וְלַחוּץ, טָהוֹר. הָיוּ שָׁווֹת, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, חוֹלְקִין הָאֶמְצָעִית. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, הַכֹּל טָהוֹר. כְּלֵי חֶרֶס, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה, מִשֶּׁיִּצָּרְפוּ בַכִּבְשָׁן, וְהִיא גְמַר מְלַאכְתָּן:
